meta.note: Canonical input layer. The interactive page and the Excel workbook are both generated from this file, so they cannot disagree. Every input carries a provenance tag.

MEASURED.label: Measured
MEASURED.desc: I timed it or counted it myself.

OBSERVED.label: Observed
OBSERVED.desc: I can see it in a firm system, or I was told it directly.

BENCHMARK.label: Benchmark
BENCHMARK.desc: Published industry source, cited with source and year.

ESTIMATED.label: Estimated
ESTIMATED.desc: My own judgement, stated as a range.

PLACEHOLDER.label: Placeholder
PLACEHOLDER.desc: Not yet filled in. The model runs, but this number is fake.

labels._note: ANONYMISE swaps these two columns. The published version ships with 'real' identical to 'anon' so nothing identifying is ever published. Fill the 'real' column in on your local copy only.

benefits_load.name: Benefits and payroll load
benefits_load.src: US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Employer Costs for Employee Compensation. Benefits run about 29-31% of total compensation for private industry, i.e. roughly a 40-45% load on wages; finance and insurance sits near the top of that band. 25% is a deliberately conservative load covering payroll taxes, health and retirement only.
benefits_load.who: The principal, or whoever handles payroll, can give the real loaded figure.

productive_hours_year.name: Productive hours per person per year
productive_hours_year.src: 2,080 scheduled hours less PTO, holidays, sick time, training and internal admin. Range I would defend: 1,600-1,800.
productive_hours_year.who: The principal can confirm the PTO and holiday policy; the rest is my judgement.

growth_rate_households.name: Household growth rate per year
growth_rate_households.src: My impression of the last few quarters of new-client activity. Not verified against a count.
growth_rate_households.who: The principal, or a new-account count out of the CRM for the last three years.

switching_uplift.name: Switching and interruption uplift
switching_uplift.src: A timed task measures the task, not the day. Real operations days carry context-switching, interruptions, rework and queue time that no task timing captures. 25% is my judgement; range 15-40%. Set it to 0% to see catalogued task time alone.
switching_uplift.who: Nobody can confirm this directly. It is the assumption most worth arguing about.

firm_overhead_per_household.name: Non-payroll firm overhead per household per year
firm_overhead_per_household.src: NOT FILLED IN. Should cover rent, technology stack, custodial platform fees, E&O, compliance vendors, professional fees, marketing, divided by household count. I cannot see the expense lines.
firm_overhead_per_household.who: The principal. This is the single number that decides whether the bottom tier looks profitable or not - do not present tier economics without it.

fee_realisation.name: Fee realisation against schedule
fee_realisation.src: NOT FILLED IN. Assumed every household pays the published schedule with no discount, no family aggregation and no flat-fee exception. That is almost certainly not true.
fee_realisation.who: The billing run from the last quarterly cycle: actual fees billed divided by fees the schedule implies.

consultant_departure_days.name: Days until the operations consultant leaves

ops_seat_comp.name: Compensation for an operations manager seat
ops_seat_comp.src: NOT FILLED IN. My guess at the market rate for an operations manager at a firm this size.
ops_seat_comp.who: The principal. A compensation study (Schwab RIA Benchmarking, Investment News Adviser Compensation) would give a defensible band.

backfill_consultant_cost.name: Annual cost to backfill the consultant like-for-like
backfill_consultant_cost.src: NOT FILLED IN. Assumed a replacement consultant costs what the current one costs.
backfill_consultant_cost.who: The principal knows the current engagement cost. A replacement quote would be a real number.

service_failure_cost_per_event.name: Cost of one service failure
service_failure_cost_per_event.src: NOT FILLED IN. A missed RMD penalty, a late transfer, a billing error and a blown deadline all cost different amounts.
service_failure_cost_per_event.who: The principal, or the compliance file of past incidents.

service_failures_avoided.name: Service failures avoided per year by the seat
service_failures_avoided.src: DELIBERATELY ZERO. I have no incident list, so I am counting nothing. Leaving this at zero makes the case for the seat weaker and honest. Raise it only against real incidents someone can name.
service_failures_avoided.who: The principal or the consultant can name actual incidents from the last two years.

paraplanning_backfill_comp.name: Compensation for a junior seat to absorb displaced paraplanning work
paraplanning_backfill_comp.src: NOT FILLED IN. My guess at a client service or associate paraplanner salary. Only relevant if the operations seat happens and the planning work I do now has to go somewhere.

advisor_hour_basis.name: How an advisor hour is valued
advisor_hour_basis.src: Two options: 'loaded_cost' values a returned advisor hour at what it costs the firm (conservative, hard to argue with) or 'revenue_capacity' values it at revenue per advisor hour (larger, and it invites the challenge that the hour would not actually have been sold). Defaulting to loaded cost on purpose.
advisor_hour_basis.who: This is a framing choice, not a fact. Ask the principal which he finds credible.

roster.comp_src: NOT FILLED IN. Principal compensation is a guess and is probably wrong; owner comp is often taken as distribution rather than salary.
roster.who: The principal. Do not push on this one - use a range if he prefers.

roster.comp_src: My own compensation. The 35% operations allocation is my estimate of my own week; the rest is plan work and research.
roster.who: Me. I can make the allocation MEASURED by keeping a two-week time log.

roster.comp_src: NOT FILLED IN. My guess at a client service associate salary.
NOT FILLED IN. My guess. The 50% operations allocation excludes bookkeeping, HR, facilities and reception.
NOT FILLED IN. Engagement cost is a guess. 0.38 FTE is roughly 12-13 hours a week, which is my impression of her time here, not a contracted figure.
roster.who: The principal holds the engagement letter. Her contracted hours are the second most important number in this model.

book.label: Under $250k
book.src: Household count and average balance read off the portfolio system household report. Accounts per household is my estimate from browsing the list, not a count.
book.who: Me - the accounts-per-household figure becomes MEASURED the moment I export an account list and divide.

book.label: $250k - $1m
book.src: Portfolio system household report. Accounts per household estimated.

book.label: $1m - $3m
book.src: Portfolio system household report. Accounts per household estimated.

book.label: Over $3m
book.src: Portfolio system household report. Accounts per household estimated.

book_meta.new_mix_src: How new households distribute across the tiers. My impression is that new business skews to T3. Not verified.
book_meta.new_mix_who: The principal, or a CRM report of households opened in the last 24 months by opening balance.

fee_schedule.src: The published fee schedule. Read off the ADV Part 2A / the client agreement.
fee_schedule.who: The principal, or the ADV itself.
fee_schedule.basis_note: TIERED / MARGINAL. Each band is charged at its own rate on the portion of assets falling inside that band. This is NOT a flat rate applied to total assets.

tasks.task: Quarterly billing cycle: calculate, review, submit
Compliance calendar items (books and records, testing)
Annual ADV amendment, delivery and filing
CRM hygiene sweep (data audit, workflow cleanup)
Trade error review and correction log
Operations standing agenda in the team meeting
Custodian document requests and statement retrieval
Cost basis and tax document checks (1099 season)
Onboarding paperwork prep and e-sign packet
ACAT / transfer initiation and tracking to completion
Data entry: CRM, planning software, portfolio system
Welcome sequence, vault and portal credentials
Quarterly report package delivery and questions
Client requests routed to an advisor instead of service

task_meta.seed_note: Every row is seeded PLACEHOLDER. The shape of the catalogue is real RIA operations work; the minutes are not. Replace each figure with a median of three timed runs and change the tag to MEASURED. That column is the strongest evidence in this model.

basis_note.firm: Fixed firm-level work. Does not scale with household count.
basis_note.household: Per household per year, for the tiers listed.
basis_note.account: Per account per year. Multiplied by accounts per household for the tiers listed.
basis_note.new_household: Per newly onboarded household. Scales with the growth rate, not the book.

work_type_note.operations: Operations work. Counts against operations capacity no matter who currently does it - including rows an advisor currently absorbs.
work_type_note.advisory: Advisory work. Does NOT count against operations capacity. Used only for the fully loaded cost-to-serve view.
